we propose a novel framework to construct adaptive receptive field (ARF) for graph convolutional networks, where ARFs enable the model to explore long-distance dependencies efficiently and robustly in graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for graph convolutions, the discrete selection of nodes is a more promising direction than the continuous weighting of nodes, as the former is less vulnerable to over-smoothing.
, for GCNs, it is beneficial to select a subset of nodes in a graph for conducting convolutions, rather than to attend to all nodes in a graph.
, in graph neural networks, the selection of receptive fields can be a more effective way to model graph dependencies.
